chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The Mutamatti' (one performing Hajj al-Tamattu') cuts off the Talbiyah when he looks at the houses of Mecca."

key_terms.اَلتَّلْبِيَةَ: The Talbiyah, the ritual recitation of 'Labbayk Allahumma labbayk' during Hajj/Umrah.
key_terms.اَلْمُتَمَتِّعُ: The Mutamatti', a pilgrim who performs Umrah and then Hajj in the same season, ending Ihram after Umrah.
key_terms.بُيُوتِ مَكَّةَ: The houses of Mecca, referring to the Kaaba and its surrounding structures, signifying the arrival point for ending Ihram.

ai.seo_question: When does a Mutamatti' pilgrim stop reciting the Talbiyah during Hajj?
ai.summary: In the Shia jurisprudential tradition, this narration from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the precise moment the Mutamatti' transitions from the Umrah rite to the Hajj rite, distinguishing it from the Qarini who maintains Talbiyah until entering the Haram. This ruling underscores the distinct legal status of the Mutamatti' as having completed the minor pilgrimage, thereby requiring a new intention and state of Ihram for the major pilgrimage. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on the physical entry into Mecca as the definitive marker for concluding the Umrah obligations.
